html:
SMTO-BOOT-0037 — The model server took too long to start

GUID: 63300805-075c-4bac-869a-750ad982a3f3
Slug: boot-model-startup-timeout
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • The model server the benchmark started wasn't ready within the time allowed (15 minutes unless you changed it). The benchmark stopped it, skipped this model and moved on to the next one.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the file in src/vllm/results/ that has this model's name and ends in .server.log, and read the last lines. It shows whether the server was still downloading or loading the model, or was stuck on an error.
  2. If it was still downloading or loading, run the benchmark again for just this model (only its name after --models) and add --startup-timeout 1800 to allow 30 minutes. Large models can take longer than 15 minutes the first time; downloaded files are kept, so later starts are faster.
  3. If the log shows an error such as running out of memory, fix that first. If it shows the server started with a different model name, run unset MODEL_ID before trying again. More time won't help a server that is stuck on an error or has loaded a model the benchmark isn't waiting for.
  4. Before trying again, run nvidia-smi and make sure no leftover model server is still using the graphics card. A second copy loading at the same time would compete for the same graphics memory.

What success looks like

  • The model becomes ready within the time allowed and the report shows a score for it.

If it still fails

  • Send this model's section of the benchmark report and its .server.log file to the person who maintains your model setup. Don't delete the downloaded model files to speed things up; they would just be downloaded again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The benchmark's launched profile did not report its model on /v1/models within --startup-timeout (default 900 s), so the benchmark stopped the process group and scored the profile as a startup failure.

What this means

  • Benchmark launch's startup deadline expires without an acceptable models response and enters its owned-process cleanup path. Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.

Why this can happen

  • Benchmark launch's startup deadline expires without an acceptable models response and enters its owned-process cleanup path.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the owned launch log and cleanup/process state before extending time or starting another server.

How to fix it

  • Read the profile's .server.log in src/vllm/results/ to tell slow progress (weight download into HF_HOME, compilation, model loading) from a stall or error. If it was progressing, rerun that profile alone with a larger --startup-timeout; otherwise fix the logged cause. launch_profile also keeps waiting until this deadline when /v1/models lists only other model IDs, so check for an exported MODEL_ID overriding the start script. Before relaunching, confirm with nvidia-smi that the stopped process group released GPU memory.
  • Inspect the named launcher log for progress or failure before changing a deadline or starting another process.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended launch becomes ready under an appropriate supported allowance without duplicate processes.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
